column3: Thomson problem: the feasible region contains coincident-point configurations where the Coulomb objective is +inf. Folded in as an obj<=bound soft constraint, that violation clamps to ~1e30 and absorbs the real constraints' O(1) terms in floating point, so the search loses the feasibility signal. Verified: dropping the objective makes this instance feasible in 20s at violation 0. Tracked in #100.

Requires changing x0 and the product x1*x2 together in 420.169*sqrt(x0^2+900) == x2*x0*x1. While x0=0 the product term vanishes so x1 and x2 get no gradient signal, and no single-variable jump improves; escaping needs a compound move. Not a defect.

Rows C1-C3 are degree-7 polynomials (x-1)(x-2)(x-3)(x-5)(x-8)(x-10)(x-12)==0 restricting each integer to {1,2,3,5,8,10,12}. Moving between allowed values crosses forbidden integers where the violation spikes into the thousands, so single-variable moves face a large barrier. Not a defect.
